forecaster_note: Short offshore window at dawn then the southerly takes over. An ENE windswell at 55° is the only thing with shape this morning, sitting under a messy 4s S windchop — 134 kJ average, so it's thin. W offshore at 9 km/h until roughly 8am, then the wind swings S and builds to 27 km/h gusting 35 by midday and everything goes to bump. The real story is Thursday: energy triples to 332 kJ on a 6.7ft 9s swell from 182°, and Saturday peaks near 972 kJ. — Derived from Surfline forecast data (surf, wind, rating, tide and weather endpoints); Surfline's written forecaster commentary was not reachable this run.

wind.summary: W 9 km/h gusting 21 at dawn — offshore everywhere. Swings SSW–S from about 8–9am and builds hard: 27 km/h gusting 35 by midday. Surf before 8am or don't bother.

shark.summary: No shark detections on the Northern Beaches in the last 24h — nothing at Dee Why, Long Reef, Curl Curl or Manly. Five statewide detections in that window, all well north (One Mile Beach, Hungry Head, Evans Head). Feed confirmed live — latest statewide detection 18h old.

days.label: Today
days.note: Dawn patrol or nothing. W offshore at 9 km/h holds until about 8am on a 4.1ft 8s ENE windswell — the angle Dee Why wants, but only 134 kJ behind it and a 3.6ft 4s S windchop sitting on top. From 9am the southerly fills in and by midday it's 27 km/h gusting 35 and blown out at all four. Manly holds on longest.

dee-why.window: 6:30–8am, hard stop. Offshore W and a filling tide to the 7:15am high. Rating drops to poor-to-fair by 9am and poor by 3pm.
alerts: Wind swings S from ~9am and builds to 27 km/h gusting 35 by midday — blown out after that
3.6ft of 4s S windchop riding over the ENE swell — expect crossed-up, lumpy faces

tip.label: Frontside at the Point
tip.text: ENE at 55° sits right in your 30–80° band, so the Point rights will be the cleanest thing going — frontside for you. But 134 kJ on an 8s period is thin: sit deep, paddle for the sets, and don't expect the bay to deliver. Volume under your feet helps here.

long-reef.window: 6:30–8am. Biggest of the four on the ENE angle, but goes onshore S by 9am and rates poor from midday.

tip.label: Most size, shortest window
tip.text: The reef converts the 8s ENE better than the beaches — 3–5ft vs Dee Why's 2–3ft. Same 134 kJ though, so it's size without punch. Worth it only if you're in the water by 6:30.

curl-curl.window: 6:30–8am. Banks will decide it — look for a corner before you park.
alerts: Onshore S from 9am, poor by midday

tip.label: Bank-dependent
tip.text: Same swell, more open to the ENE than Dee Why so it picks up size, but the 4s S chop shows up worse on an open beach. Drive-by from the headland first.

manly.window: 6:30–11am — longest window of the four. The S change stays offshore at North Steyne until roughly midday, so it holds shape while everything north is already bumpy.
alerts: Smallest of the four on this ENE angle

tip.label: Best rating today
tip.text: Only spot still rating fair at 9am. Smallest size, but the S change is offshore here rather than side-on — if you can't make dawn at Dee Why, this is the call. Southern corner toward Queenscliff for the lefts (backside for you).

days.label: Tomorrow
days.note: Big jump — 332 kJ average and 6.7ft at 9s, but it's from 182°, dead south. That's the angle Dee Why wraps badly, so expect it to under-deliver at the Point and over-deliver at Long Reef and Curl Curl. Wind stays light all day (8–12 km/h) and only turns onshore E–SE after midday. Morning is the play.

dee-why.window: Dawn–11am on light SSW. Rates fair all day — the 182° angle is the problem, not the wind.
alerts: Primary swell at 182° is dead south — wraps poorly into Dee Why, expect it to feel smaller than the numbers

long-reef.window: Dawn–noon. Pick of the four on a S angle — biggest and most exposed. Wind is onshore but only 9–10 km/h, so it stays workable.
alerts: 5–8ft with 332 kJ — solid. Pick your board accordingly

curl-curl.window: Dawn–10am while the SSW is still side-off. Real size on this S swell and less raw than Long Reef.

manly.window: All morning, but heavily shadowed — 2–4ft off a 6.7ft swell. Only worth it if you want the smallest option.

days.label: Weekend
days.note: Two very different days. SATURDAY: big — 508 kJ average peaking near 972 kJ, 5.7ft at 9s from 173° with a 2.4ft E component, light cross winds and a brief W offshore lull around midday. SUNDAY: drops to 200 kJ but the wind goes W offshore at 6 km/h from dawn to 9am — cleanest conditions of the week, and Long Reef rates fair-to-good. If you're picking one mid-morning session, Sunday.

dee-why.window: SATURDAY: 3–6ft chest to head, cross S wind with an offshore lull near midday — that's the window. SUNDAY: 2–4ft on W offshore 6 km/h dawn to 9am, cleanest of the two but only 200 kJ.
alerts: Saturday's primary is 173° — still a poor wrap angle for Dee Why; Sunday is the same story but the offshore makes up for it

long-reef.window: SATURDAY: 4–8ft and heavy — 972 kJ peak, cross-shore S. SUNDAY: 4–6ft with W offshore and the only fair-to-good rating in the whole outlook, 6–9am. That's the session.
alerts: Saturday peaks near 972 kJ — serious water. Sunday morning is the smarter call

curl-curl.window: SATURDAY: 3–7ft, bank-dependent, cross S. SUNDAY: 3–5ft clean on the W offshore — solid backup to Long Reef.

manly.window: Shadowed both days — 2–4ft. The sheltered fallback if Saturday's size is too much north of here.
